description: The webview permissions the frontend uses, on every platform: it listens for backend events and drives its own title bar (minimise, maximise, close, drag) and widens the window when a tool pane opens. Everything else goes through the app's own commands, and only those listed in permissions/ui-commands.toml (granted here as ui-commands): with that file present Tauri refuses any other application command. Desktop-only permissions (window-state plugin) live in capabilities/desktop.json so the Android build doesn't fail validation when that plugin isn't compiled in. shell, opener, fs and webview permissions are deliberately absent, and so are the broad core:default set and the path/app/image/menu/tray/resources APIs, which the app never calls: exposing them only widens what a compromised webview could do.
